# The selected dirty SDIRK7 coefficient field has degree 324 and a real place

The [19-adic lifting packet](../strict-sdirk7-unpaid-head/README.md)
isolates a strict nine-stage, exact-order-seven tableau in a fixed
five-equation cubic-dirty slice. The fixed second reflected clock is
zero, the third is four, and the first normalized tap is \(1/2\).
Its residue in the variable order \((z,a,b_*,c_*,h)\) is
\((8,9,15,7,5)\) in \(\mathbb F_{19}\). Here \(z=1/\gamma\)
and the six reflected tail clocks are \(a,b_*,c_*,4,0,1\).

**For this exact point, the field generated by the tableau is
\(\mathbb Q(z)\), of degree 324.** Its minimal polynomial is the
literal integer coefficient list
[primitive-z-degree-324.json](primitive-z-degree-324.json)
(in increasing degree). It has a real root; the associated
real embedding gives precisely the [previously isolated real
tableau](../strict-sdirk7-real-dirty/README.md). In particular
all the nonzero reconstruction pivots, the visible cubic defect,
the genuinely unpaid third axis, and the eighth-bush obstruction
hold at this real embedding.

No rational point of these same fixed five equations with all
coordinates integral at 19 can reduce to \((8,9,15,7,5)\).
The unit Jacobian gives only one 19-adic lift of the residue, and
that lift has the stated nontrivial number field. Neither other
residues or slices, nor the global rational nine-stage question,
are resolved here.

## Exact elimination and the primitive coordinate

Put \(c=c_*\), \(s=a+b_*\), \(p=ab_*\),
\[
 R_0(X)=X(X-1)(X-4)(X-c),\qquad
 Q(X)=X^2-sX+p,\qquad P(X)=R_0(X)Q(X).
\]
The normalized integration functional is \(I_z(X^j)=z^j/(j+1)\).
Define the moment polynomial
\[
 K(X)=I_{z,T}\!\left(\frac{P(T)-P(X)}{T-X}\right).
\]
At each tail node \(y\), the weight is \(K(y)/P'(y)\).
The first two equations eliminate two variables:
\[
 p=\frac{s I_z(XR_0)-I_z(X^2R_0)}{I_z(R_0)},\qquad
 h=\frac{4K(4)+2K(1)}{K(4)+3K(0)+2K(1)} .
\]
Their denominators are nonzero on the selected residue. The affine
polynomial \(W\) has \(W(0)=-hK(0)\) and
\(W(1)=-(1-h)K(1)/2\). The third equation is
\[
 2(c+3)W(c)+(c^3-9c^2+18c-6)(c-h)K(c)=0.
\]
After clearing known unit scales, its surviving factor \(F_3(z,c,s)\)
has total degree 13 and is quadratic in \(s\), with nonzero leading
coefficient at \(z=8,c=7\) modulo 19.

For the fourth equation, let \(U\) of degree at most five be the
interpolant of \(W(y)^2/K(y)\) on the six nodes. The isotropy equation
is \(\sum_y U(y)/P'(y)=0\); equivalently its degree-five coefficient
vanishes. Thus \(U=J_3+R_0 V\) where \(J_3\) is the cubic interpolant
of \(W^2/K\) at \(0,1,4,c\) and \(V\) is constant in \(X\).
Modulo \(Q\), write
\[
 A_0+A_1 X = K R_0 \bmod Q,\qquad
 B_0+B_1 X = (W^2-KJ_3)\bmod Q.
\]
Choose the nonzero \(A_0\) port. Thus \(V=B_0/A_0\) and the fourth
equation is \(A_0 B_1-A_1 B_0=0\), with surviving numerator
\(F_4(z,c,s)\) of total degree 23. The generator checks each divided
factor at the selected residue. The actual quadratic for \(s\)
has the two residues 4 and 5 at \(z=8,c=7\); the former fails the
fourth equation.

The fifth equation is also linearizable on the same quadratic.
Indeed \(D_3=W(h)/P(h)\) by interpolation; the third cubic
value \(v_3\) is \(U(h)/W(h)\) by the same interpolation applied
to \(Dv=0\). Write \(w=z-h,\ \eta=(w+2)/(3w-1)\), and
\(q(X)=(X-w)(X-\eta)\), with \(Jq\) its primitive from zero.
The chronological fifth equation is equivalent to the vanishing,
at \(X=a\), of
\[
 \bigl(q(z-X)-Jq(z-X)\bigr)K(X)U(h)+Jq(w)W(X)W(h).
\]
Reduce this expression modulo \(Q(X)\) and clear only tested
nonzero scales. Call the resulting form \(N_0+N_1 X\).
In the generated certificate \((N_0,N_1)=(9,18)\bmod19\)
at \((z,c,s)=(8,7,5)\), so it recovers \(a=-N_0/N_1\), with
residue 9. The fifth eliminated polynomial \(F_5\) is obtained
by plugging this expression into \(Q(a)=0\).

Reduce \(F_4,F_5\) modulo the quadratic \(F_3\) in \(s\), and
write their cleared remainders as \(l_0+l_1s\) and \(m_0+m_1s\).
The selected residue gives \((l_0,l_1)=(18,4)\), so \(s=-l_0/l_1\).
Use \(S=l_1m_0-l_0m_1\) and the uniquely selected factor \(R\)
of \(\operatorname{Res}_s(F_3,F_4)\). These are two polynomials
in \((z,c)\), vanishing at the selected point. The choice of \(R\)
discards only factors nonzero at the mod-19 residue. It has
bidegree \((21,9)\), while \(S\) has bidegree \((254,81)\).

All five tableau coordinates are already rational functions of
\((z,c)\). Conversely, the tableau's diagonal and row sums give
back \(z\) and the normalized reflected clocks, so this is an
equality of generated fields. To remove \(c\), specialize
\(z=8\bmod19\), where the leading \(c\)-coefficient of \(R\)
is 11, and check \(\gcd(R(8,c),S(8,c))=c+12\) in
\(\mathbb F_{19}[c]\). In the rank-nine \(c\)-algebra obtained by
making \(R\) monic, multiplication by \(S\) therefore has
nullity one over \(\mathbb F_{19}\). The same matrix at the lifted
\(z\) has rank at least eight (the nonzero minor survives) and
has a common root \(c\). Thus the common gcd over \(\mathbb Q(z)\)
is linear, since extending scalars to \(\mathbb Q_{19}\) cannot
change its degree. This proves \(c\in\mathbb Q(z)\).

## Bounded CRT and independent degree check

Let \(O(Z)\) be the determinant resultant
\(\operatorname{Res}_c(R,S)\) of the primitive integer
representatives. Its Sylvester size is 90, with 81 shifted rows
of \(R\) and 9 of \(S\). If \(\|\cdot\|_1\) denotes the sum of
absolute values of all integer coefficients, then the Leibniz
formula and submultiplicativity bound every resultant coefficient
by
\[
 90!\ \|R\|_1^{81}\ \|S\|_1^9.
\]
The program checks the stated degrees and bound from the actual
inputs, giving a conservative threshold of 11540 bits. It
computes the resultant at separately trial-division-checked
primes (rejecting degree drops in the input \(c\)-degrees),
and reconstructs signed coefficients uniquely after the
combined modulus exceeds twice the bound. The recorded run
uses 408 primes, a modulus of bitlength 11833, and produces a
degree-3691 integer polynomial. This is not an extrapolation
from agreeing residues.

Writing \(H\) for the literal degree-324 polynomial, the script
checks exactly that \(O/H\) is integral and \(H\) divides \(O\).
The selected residues are \(H(8)=0\) and \((O/H)(8)=4\bmod19\)
(\(O'(8)=17\bmod19\)). Consequently the 19-adic point is a
root of \(H\), since the complementary factor is a unit there.

A separate checker verifies irreducibility without relying
on the rational factorizer. It multiplies the six literal
finite-field factorizations for primes \(11,17,23,37,43,71\),
checks each factor by the Frobenius/Rabin irreducibility test,
and intersects the resulting sets of possible factor degrees.
The intersection is exactly \(\{0,324\}\). The leading
coefficient has full degree in all six reductions, so any
proper rational factor would give a prohibited intermediate
degree. Thus \(H\) is the minimal polynomial at the selected
19-adic point.

## Exact real embedding and identification

At the real interval from the isolated five-coordinate box,
the same literal \(H\) has opposite signs at the exact rational
endpoints of the radius-\(10^{-30}\) \(z\)-interval. Its derivative
is positive throughout, certified by the value at the center and an
absolute-coefficient bound on the second derivative. Thus the
interval contains a unique simple real root \(\zeta\). Sending
\(z\) to \(\zeta\) gives a real embedding of the same degree-324
field. A field embedding preserves each nonzero pivot, the
strict diagonal, and each reviewed rooted order condition and
nonzero residual.

The identification replay also checks that every scale or factor
canceled in the elimination stays nonzero on the separately
certified real box. Thus that point satisfies \(R=S=0\).
The checker proves the full complementary projection \(O/H\)
stays nonzero on its \(z\)-interval, by applying exact derivative
majorants to its squarefree layers. The certified real point
therefore has \(H(z)=0\) and \(z=\zeta\). The linear common-root
recovery of \(c\) over the field transports to this embedding,
and the remaining coordinates and tableau follow from the same
rational formulas. The earlier real-box pivots and exact signs
belong to this very embedding.

## Replay scope

The exact algebra scripts use Python and **python-flint 0.8.0**,
installed in the scratch replay. There are no Sage, SymPy,
Singular, or network dependencies in the scripts. From this
directory run:

    python3 check-irreducible-and-real.py
    python3 eliminate-chart.py
    python3 build-two-coordinate.py
    python3 reconstruct-projection.py --workers 3 --save-full
    python3 check-real-identification.py

The first three checks take under ten seconds in the original
execution. The bounded CRT took about 80 seconds with three
workers. Generated work files include the full projection used
by the last check; they are not inputs trusted for the CRT.
The CRT replay starts from scratch. Use the common work-dir
option to keep intermediate files out of the source directory.

The native
[SDIRKSevenDirtyDegreeReceipt.lean](../../lean/RKCert/Research/SDIRKSevenDirtyDegreeReceipt.lean)
certifies the factor-degree intersection and the generic
signed-CRT uniqueness rule, checked on stock Lean 4.36.0.
[projection-audit.lean](projection-audit.lean) gives the typed
audit. The elimination, resultants, individual finite
polynomial factorizations and interval proofs are exact
independent arithmetic/mathematical proofs, not a claim that
the entire number-field certificate is already native Lean.
